description: A six-panel schematic composite showing how microstructure evolves with intercritical annealing. Panels are circular fields (whole prior-austenite grains) arranged in two rows, read in the order set by thick black arrows: (a) HRQ → (b) IA750_5 Min → (c) IA750_30 Min → (d) IA750_60 Min (arrow labelled IA750_30 Min) → (e) IA750_120 Min → (f) IA750_180 Min. Every circle is subdivided by jagged white δ (delta ferrite) grains that enclose a grey central region labelled γ° (untransformed austenite). (a) HRQ additionally holds orange angular α′ martensite plates (three, labelled α′). From (b) onward the former martensite region contains fine blue parallel needle-shaped γ^rev (reverted austenite) alongside dark-grey α intercritical ferrite, both pointed to by arrows. The abundance and sharpness of blue γ^rev needles is greatest at 5 min and declines progressively through (c)–(f), the fewest being in (f); unlabelled yellow (c), green (d) and orange (e, f) line features plus small red dashed marks (b, c) appear with no printed colour legend. The figure argues that longer annealing partitions austenite stabilisers into γ°, making reverted austenite leaner, less mechanically stable and finally dissolved.

subfigures.description: Circle labelled HRQ: white jagged δ ferrite grains enclose a grey region labelled γ° (untransformed austenite) containing three angular orange α′ martensite plates, each labelled α′.

Circle labelled IA750_5 Min: the grey γ° region now contains dense fine blue parallel needle-shaped γ^rev with arrows labelled α and γ^rev, plus small red dashed marks; orange α′ is no longer present.
Circle labelled IA750_30 Min: similar needle-shaped blue γ^rev packet, slightly fewer needles than (b), with a yellow line feature inside the transformed region.
Circle labelled IA750_60 Min: fewer, less sharp blue γ^rev needles; a green line feature appears where yellow was in (c).
Circle labelled IA750_120 Min: further reduced blue γ^rev needle content, with orange needle/line features within the grey region.
Circle labelled IA750_180 Min: the fewest blue γ^rev needles of the series, with prominent orange needle/line features; arrows still label α and γ^rev.

observations.observation: The figure is a six-circle schematic; thick black arrows define the reading sequence (a)→(b)→(c)→(d)→(e)→(f), i.e. increasing intercritical annealing time.
Sample/condition labels printed beneath the circles are HRQ, IA750_5 Min, IA750_30 Min, IA750_60 Min, IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min.
The arrow between panels (c) and (d) carries the text 'IA750_30 Min'.
White jagged grains in all six circles are labelled δ; the grey central region is labelled γ° in all six circles.
Panel (a) HRQ contains three orange angular plates labelled α′ (martensite); no such orange plates exist in panels (b)–(f).
Panels (b)–(f) show blue parallel needle-shaped features labelled γ^rev together with an arrow-labelled α within the grey γ° region.
The number and length of blue γ^rev needles is largest in (b) IA750_5 Min and decreases monotonically through (c), (d), (e) to a minimum in (f) IA750_180 Min.
Unlabelled yellow (c), green (d) and orange (e, f) line/needle features occur inside the transformed region, and small red dashed marks occur in (b) and (c); no colour key is printed in the figure.

The caption states the schematic represents dissolution/transformation of martensite (α′) present in hot rolled & quenched (HRO) specimen into reverted austenite (γ rev) and intercritical ferrite (α) during intercritical annealing at 750 °C for different durations (δ-delta ferrite, γ° untransformed austenite).
The citing text states that after 5 minutes at 750 °C martensite transforms to sharp needle-shaped austenite with α-ferrite adjacent to it, as shown in Fig. 8(b).
The citing text states that with increasing annealing time the sharpness of reverted austenite is reduced and some globular-shaped reverted austenite can be seen in Fig. 8(c, d).

The citing text states the globular reverted austenite has an average diameter of 0.0185±0.010 µm and that at 60 min annealing the needle and globular reverted austenite has optimum mechanical stability leading to an enhanced TRIP effect.

The citing text states that at 180 minutes there is complete dissolution of reverted austenite through elemental partitioning of Mn and Al to adjacent untransformed austenite, giving a low TRIP effect.

The citing text states that the fraction of reverted austenite decreases with further heating to 120 and 180 min (Fig. 8(e-f)), reducing the overall retained austenite fraction and the austenite transformation ratio.

unreadable_items: No colour legend/key is printed, so the meaning of the yellow (c), green (d) and orange (e, f) line features is not stated in the figure
The small red dashed marks in panels (b) and (c) are not defined by the caption or by any in-figure label
The caption uses both 'HRO' and the panel label 'HRQ' for the hot rolled & quenched condition; the panel label reads HRQ
Individual needle dimensions in panels (b)-(f) are below the scale resolvable in the supplied rendering
